1995.kid: A tall metal mast with thin aerials at the top. Its radios share each wave between eight phones, taking turns, and send every call down a line to the controller box.
1995.nerd: A GSM base station (BTS) on 900 MHz: a lattice mast with sector aerials and a few transceivers in the cabinet, one 200 kHz carrier each, eight time slots per carrier. It sends each call on over Abis, unopened.

peek.kid: The mast doesn’t open your parcel. It catches your phone’s radio turn and passes what was in it on down the line.
peek.nerd: The BTS ends the radio burst and the channel coding and passes the call’s RLP frames on in a 16 kbit/s sub-slot; nothing here reads PPP or IP.
